results.label: Proved here
results.text: Theorem 25 (floor for one-band hybrid supports): a one-band Stadlmann support with A1 ≤ 1/4 + omega, any delta, any caps and any minorant can give DHL[k,2] only if M_k(4(A1+eps), 4(A1-eps)) > 4. Certified false for every eps: k ≤ 29 (omega = 0), k ≤ 28 (omega = 0.003 and 1/300, Stadlmann's level), k ≤ 26 (omega = 0.007, the level of Charton et al.), k ≤ 22 (omega ≤ 1/68). Reduction proved; table Computed in interval arithmetic and re-checked with a second library. Far from 49 and 45; it ignores the caps.

results.label: Computed
results.text: Stadlmann's capped support at k = 49 (his parameters, re-read in the source): with F = P 1_T, P of degree 20 (707 coefficients), the criterion ratio is ≥ 3.95972, below the 4 needed. The 240 rung is NOT reproduced. The loss comes from bounding the capped marginals by Cauchy-Schwarz (Proposition 23), not from the caps themselves.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Proposition 23: for F = P 1_T, I_T ≤ I(P) and J_T ≥ J(P) − 2 sqrt(J(P) L E(P)), where E(P) is an exact union bound for the integral of P^2 over the cap-violation set; the pieces {m coordinates above delta, their sum above the cap} are integrated exactly with shifted power sums (checked against Lemma 3 and against sympy for k = 3).

results.label: Computed
results.text: Cap-free parts of the 2026 supports: M_{49,15/506} ≥ 3.9685535 (degree 20) and M_{45,8/257} ≥ 3.9029887 (degree 21, dimension 846, equal to the dimension stated by Charton et al.), so by dilation the cap-free ratios are ≥ 4.016176 (Stadlmann's (L, tau) = (1.042, 0.982)) and ≥ 4.012272 (Charton et al.'s (1.06, 0.996)). Compared with their claimed capped value 4.00438, the caps seem to cost about 0.008 at k = 45 (a comparison, not a verification).

results.text: Counting large coordinates: if every entry of a list exceeds g then length × g ≤ sum; so (in units of 1/1000) at most 9 coordinates of a point of Stadlmann's support exceed 4 delta = 112, and 7 such coordinates always exceed every cap (680).

results.text: M_{50,1/25} ≥ 4.0012466 (degree 25, 1780 coefficients) and ≥ 4.0043063 (degree 27, 2526 coefficients) on Polymath8b's epsilon-enlarged simplex, even power sums. With the Lean tuple (50, 246), Bombieri-Vinogradov and Polymath8b Thm 3.12(i) this gives H1 ≤ 246 end to end, the established bound. Agrees with Polymath8b's 4.00124 (d=25) and 4.0043 (d=27) to every printed digit; Gram formulas checked against direct sympy integration. Reproduction, not new.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Exponential-moment formula: integrals of (1-P1)^A times products of power sums over the simplex are A!/(k+A+w)! times E[prod P_j(X)^b_j] for iid Exp(1) variables, an integer given by an EGF power (Lemma 3). Possibly folklore.

ideas.idea: Dilation identity M_k(L,tau) = 4 A1 M_{k, eps/A1} plus the two-zone dual weight, to bound the one-band hybrid supports of 2026 as a function of the level omega.
ideas.note: Theorem 25: no k ≤ 28 at Stadlmann's omega = 0.003, no k ≤ 26 at omega = 0.007, no k ≤ 22 for omega ≤ 1/68, for any delta, caps and minorant. The same weight fails at the next k.

ideas.idea: Rigorous capped ratio from a polynomial P: penalise the exact integral of P^2 over the cap-violation set in a generalised eigenproblem, bound J_T by Cauchy-Schwarz.
ideas.note: Penalty lowers E/I from 1.2e-3 to 1.6e-7, but the bound reaches only 3.9597 < 4 at degree 20 (k = 49). The Cauchy-Schwarz treatment of J_T is the bottleneck; need exact capped marginals.

ideas.idea: Union bound for the cap-violation set over m-subsets with sum above the cap, dropping the condition that each coordinate exceeds delta.
ideas.note: Hopelessly loose: E/I ≈ 146 for the cap-free optimiser at degree 20 (the m = 4..6 terms explode).

ideas.idea: Optimise Lemma 13 over ALL weights psi_m = Psi(S - t_m, t_m) (the family containing Cor. 6.4 and the two-zone weight) as a convex program, to learn the limit of this family.
ideas.note: Discretised optimum ≈ 4.14 at (k, eps) = (50, 1/25) vs truth ≥ 4.0012; equals k/(k-1) log k at eps = 0. The family cannot reach the true threshold; need weights seeing more of t (Proposition 19).

ideas.idea: Degree extrapolation of certified M_{k,eps}: does the eps-enlarged simplex reach k = 49?
ideas.note: Geometric model validated at k = 50 (optimistic by ≤ 0.0012) predicts sup_eps M_{49,eps} ≈ 3.991-3.994 < 4: heuristic evidence that the method stops at 50 (Remark 20).

ideas.idea: Collatz-Wielandt weights psi_m = (int F dt_m)/F from a positive approximate extremal F, to approach the true floor near k = 50.
ideas.note: Exact for the extremal F; the obstacle is controlling sup over t of the ratio for a polynomial F.

ideas.idea: Active-count-normalised weight (beta/n)(a − S_A + n t_m) to beat scaling at small eps.
ideas.note: Exact fiber evaluation at k = 50, eps = 1/25: never below 4.178, worse than the scaling bound 4.1515 (Remark 18).

ideas.idea: Two-zone dual weight (linear in t_m below s1, proportional to t_m/S above) in Polymath8b's Lemma 6.1 with the marginal region kept, to bound M_{k,eps} uniformly in eps.
ideas.note: Theorem 15: no k ≤ 29 for any eps < 1, beating the k ≤ 23 floor from Polymath8b Prop. 6.5.

ideas.idea: Exponential-moment generating function for simplex integrals of power-sum products, to make certified high-degree computations cheap.
ideas.note: Lemma 3. Builds a 471x471 exact Gram pair in about 15 s.

ideas.idea: Weighted pigeonhole: give the shifts unequal weights to force two primes closer than the tuple's diameter.
ideas.note: Convexity plus perfection of unit interval graphs. Proved as Proposition 8; checked numerically for k = 3.

ideas.idea: Floor of the method: a rigorous upper bound (dual certificate) for the 2026 hybrid sieve supports, to learn how far below 186 the present inputs can go.
ideas.note: eps-enlarged simplex down to k ≤ 29 (Theorem 15). Session 5: one-band hybrid supports (Stadlmann, Charton et al.) cannot reach k ≤ 28 at omega = 0.003, k ≤ 26 at omega = 0.007, whatever the caps (Theorem 25). Multi-band supports and the 186/182 constructions still open; a floor that sees the caps is next.

ideas.idea: Does the slicing lemma behind Proposition 8 survive on enlarged supports?
ideas.note: Yes: a single rescaling by (1+eps-|u|)/(1+eps) keeps each slice inside the eps-problem's J-region. Proposition 10; checked numerically for k = 3 and eps up to 1/3.

ideas.idea: Richer symmetric test functions to pass k = 102 and reach M_54 > 4 (270).
ideas.note: M_54 ≥ 4.0023860 at degree 23 (1236 coefficients): 270 reproduced. Next rung needs the enlarged simplex.

ideas.idea: One explicit bilinear hypothesis that implies twin primes, formalised in Lean.
ideas.note: Track B. Start from Bombieri's asymptotic sieve and Heath-Brown's Siegel-zero theorem.
